identity.question: can a mouth-localised detector separate speaking from silent once head motion is held constant, and how far above its own controls does it sit?
identity.dependency_note: numpy only, no scipy and no GPU: the result reproduces on the repository's own interpreter. MediaPipe is NOT used in this lane; see docs/research/MOUTH-DETECTOR.md for the cross-check.

pre_registered_rule.written_before: the measurement code in this file existed; the rule text was fixed first and the numbers were produced by the code as written
pre_registered_rule.scope: session-level speaking detection from the mouth region, on captures A (speaking, facing camera), B (speaking, facing away), C (silent, facing camera) and empty1 (no person), read at the detected NV12 stride

terms.M: the mouth-box feature (rows 46-58, cols 62-86), selected per fold by FEATURE SELECTION below
terms.C: the SAME feature computed on the CHEEK box (rows 46-58, cols 92-116), selected the same way
terms.H: the head-motion proxy: the mean absolute consecutive-frame difference over the upper-face box (rows 20-44, cols 56-104). PRIMARY covariate. H_frame (whole frame), H_shift (upper-face translation) and H_mouthshift (mouth-box translation) are reported as variants.
terms.LOO: leave-one-session-out over {A, B, C}: three folds, test sessions A, B and C in turn

pre_registered_rule.feature_selection: Inside each fold, the mouth feature is the candidate with the highest TRAINING balanced frame accuracy of the threshold classifier; ties are broken by the lower candidate index in the fixed order motion, lumafluct, histdiff, hfchange, vgradfluct, darkfracfluct. The test session is never used for selection. The cheek control and the head-motion proxy are evaluated with the identical pipeline.
pre_registered_rule.classifier: A per-frame threshold on one feature: 'speaking' iff feature > threshold. The threshold maximises balanced accuracy on the TRAINING frames. The direction is fixed (higher = speaking) for every feature, because every candidate is a magnitude. The session decision is 'speaking' iff the MAJORITY of the held-out session's frames are above the threshold.
pre_registered_rule.training_set: The two non-test sessions' frames. If those two sessions contain no silent class (which happens in exactly one fold, the fold that holds out C), the negative class is supplied by the empty room's TRAINING SLICE: frames 0..1499 of empty1.nv12, labelled silent. The empty room's frames 1500..4499 are the HELD-OUT physical control and are never trained on. A sensitivity variant that adds the empty-room negative to every fold is reported.
pre_registered_rule.primary_metrics: macro_frame_recall: the mean over the three folds of the held-out session's frame accuracy (each held-out session is single-class, so this is the recall of that session's class). loo_session_accuracy: the fraction of folds whose session decision is correct. auc_ac: the AUC of the feature separating A's frames from C's frames. conditional_auc_ac: the AUC computed WITHIN strata of H, so the head-motion proxy is held constant. residual_d_ac: Cohen's d on the feature after regressing it on H with the TRAINING sessions only.

checks.R1_survives_the_head_motion_control: The mouth signal survives the confound iff BOTH: R1a -- conditional_auc_ac for M is above 0.50 with a permutation z of at least +2.0 (2000 permutations of the session labels within the H-strata); AND R1b -- residual_d_ac for M is above 0 with a permutation z of at least +3.0 (2000 permutations of the session labels over the residualised values). If either fails, the mouth signal does NOT survive the head-motion control, whatever the classifier scores.
checks.R2_mouth_specific: The effect is mouth-specific iff conditional_auc_ac for M exceeds that for C (the cheek) by at least 0.02, with a permutation z of at least +2.0 for the paired difference.
checks.R3_beats_the_competing_predictor: The detector beats head motion iff macro_frame_recall for M exceeds that for H by at least 0.05, AND M's loo_session_accuracy is at least H's in at least 2 of the 3 folds.
checks.R4_beats_the_nulls: The detector beats the nulls iff macro_frame_recall for M exceeds EACH of: the best permuted-session-label null, the training-majority blank control, and the session-fingerprint control, by at least 0.05.
checks.R5_honesty_gate: Always reported, never a pass or a fail of the feature: the labels are session-level, so the leave-one-session-out metric is partly degenerate -- a predictor that identifies the SESSION rather than the speaking state can score 1.000, and the blank control does. No frame-level audio<->video claim is admissible from these captures (the audio and the video are independent takes). Every number in this lane is a SESSION-LEVEL statement.

pre_registered_rule.verdict_rule: The verdict is the FIRST of these that applies, and it is computed mechanically from the recorded control numbers: 1. if NOT (R1a AND R1b) -> 'mouth_signal_does_not_survive_head_motion'; 2. elif NOT R2 -> 'mouth_signal_survives_but_is_not_mouth_specific'; 3. elif NOT R3 -> 'mouth_detector_does_not_beat_head_motion'; 4. elif NOT R4 -> 'mouth_detector_beats_nothing'; 5. else -> 'mouth_detector_survives_head_motion'. If the data are insufficient to evaluate any check, the verdict is 'UNDETERMINED' and is never printed from a partial run.
pre_registered_rule.stopping_rule: Every number reported here comes from one run of this script over the four captures on disk. No threshold, no window and no permutation count was changed after the first run; the results file records the script's own SHA-256 so that any later edit is visible.

pre_registered_rule_text:
PRE-REGISTERED DECISION RULE (v1.0, 2026-10-20)

SCOPE: session-level speaking detection from the mouth region, on captures
A (speaking, facing), B (speaking, away), C (silent, facing) and empty1 (no
person), read at the detected NV12 stride.

TERMS
  M = the mouth-box feature (rows 46-58, cols 62-86), selected per fold.
  C = the same feature on the CHEEK box (rows 46-58, cols 92-116).
  H = the head-motion proxy: mean |I_t - I_{t-1}| over the upper-face box
      (rows 20-44, cols 56-104).  PRIMARY covariate.
  LOO = leave-one-session-out over {A, B, C}.

FEATURE SELECTION: inside each fold, the candidate with the highest
TRAINING balanced frame accuracy; ties broken by the lower index in the
fixed order motion, lumafluct, histdiff, hfchange, vgradfluct,
darkfracfluct.  The test session is never used for selection.

CLASSIFIER: per-frame threshold, 'speaking' iff feature > threshold, the
threshold maximising balanced accuracy on the TRAINING frames.  The session
decision is 'speaking' iff the MAJORITY of the held-out session's frames
are above the threshold.

TRAINING SET: the two non-test sessions' frames.  If those two contain no
silent class (the fold that holds out C), the negative class is the empty
room's TRAINING SLICE (frames 0..1499 of empty1, labelled silent); the
empty room's frames 1500..4499 are the held-out physical control and are
never trained on.

PRIMARY METRICS: macro_frame_recall (mean over folds of the held-out
session's frame accuracy); loo_session_accuracy; auc_ac; conditional_auc_ac
(AUC within strata of H); residual_d_ac (Cohen's d after regressing the
feature on H with the TRAINING sessions only).

R1  the mouth signal survives the head-motion control iff BOTH
    R1a  conditional_auc_ac for M > 0.50, permutation z >= +2.0
         (2000 permutations of the session labels within the H-strata)
    R1b  residual_d_ac for M > 0, permutation z >= +3.0
         (2000 permutations of the session labels)
    If either fails -> the mouth signal does NOT survive the confound,
    whatever the classifier scores.

R2  the effect is mouth-specific iff conditional_auc_ac for M exceeds that
    for C by >= 0.02, with permutation z >= +2.0 for the paired difference.

R3  the detector beats head motion iff macro_frame_recall for M exceeds that
    for H by >= 0.05, AND M's loo_session_accuracy is at least H's in at
    least 2 of the 3 folds.

R4  the detector beats the nulls iff macro_frame_recall for M exceeds EACH
    of the best permuted-session-label null, the training-majority blank
    control and the session-fingerprint control by >= 0.05.

R5  HONESTY GATE, always reported: the labels are session-level, so the
    leave-one-session-out metric is partly degenerate -- a predictor that
    identifies the SESSION rather than the speaking state can score 1.000,
    and the blank control does.  No frame-level audio<->video claim is
    admissible from these captures (independent takes).  Everything in this
    lane is a SESSION-LEVEL statement.

VERDICT: the first of these that applies, computed mechanically from the
recorded control numbers:
  1. NOT (R1a AND R1b) -> mouth_signal_does_not_survive_head_motion
  2. R1 OK but NOT R2  -> mouth_signal_survives_but_is_not_mouth_specific
  3. R1, R2 OK, NOT R3 -> mouth_detector_does_not_beat_head_motion
  4. R1..R3 OK, NOT R4 -> mouth_detector_beats_nothing
  5. otherwise          -> mouth_detector_survives_head_motion
  Insufficient data    -> UNDETERMINED (never printed from a partial run).

mouth_box.provenance: read off a 5x render with a coordinate grid (docs/research/NV12-STRIDE.md §5); consistent with the MediaPipe landmark positions in docs/research/MOUTH-APERTURE-ALIGNMENT.md §2 (upper inner lip (78.60, 52.52), lower inner lip (78.66, 53.76)), which fall inside it

cheek_box.role: spatial control, same rows, right of the mouth

fore_box.role: the upper face: the head-motion covariate's box, and a third spatial control

bg_box.role: the same rows, far to the right of the face: a pure-scene control that contains nothing of the wearer

geometry.what_each_box_contains: MEASURED, not assumed. The boxes were drawn on a 6x render of A.nv12 and the per-pixel temporal standard deviation was measured over each of them. The face's own right-hand edge is at x ~ 90 (the MediaPipe left eye corner in docs/research/MOUTH-APERTURE-ALIGNMENT.md §2 is at x=91.98), so the CHEEK control box, which starts at column 92, STRADDLES the face's silhouette rather than sitting on a cheek. It is therefore not a clean 'face but not mouth' control: a high-contrast edge that moves with the head passes through it. The bg box is the clean scene control, and the fore box is the upper face.

empty_room_control.note: the empty room carries no person, so its mouth-box motion is the floor: what a mouth region does when nobody is speaking. The held-out slice (frames 1500..4499) is never trained on.

empty_room_false_alarm.note: the false-alarm rate of each fold's detector on the empty room's HELD-OUT slice (the last 100 s of the recording), which no detector was trained on

published.note: the published figures are the ratio of the two EFFECT SIZES (0.733 / 0.477 = 1.54), not the ratio of the raw differences; the raw-difference ratio is 2.42x

blank_constant_speaking.note: a constant 'speaking' answer is exactly right on a pure speaking session, which is why it scores 1.000 on the folds whose held-out session is a speaking one

blank_training_majority.note: the training set's majority class; ties break to 'speaking'

session_fingerprint.feature: the whole frame's mean luma (illumination), per session
session_fingerprint.note: a pure session identifier: it cannot see the mouth at all. If it reaches 1.000, then a leave-one-session-out accuracy of 1.000 is not evidence of anything

permuted_session_labels.note: the session-label null has only THREE distinct draws with three sessions, so it is a sanity check, not a null distribution; the frame-label shuffle below is the distributional null

frame_label_shuffle.note: the training labels are permuted across the pooled training frames, so the training set keeps its feature values and its class balance but loses the session-label association; the held-out session is scored against the REAL label, so this is the pipeline's own optimism, measured rather than assumed

wrong_session_pairing.note: A's video is labelled silent and C's video is labelled speaking: the negative control the brief asks for. A detector that has learned 'this take is the speaking one' must fail here.

checks.headline_note: the feature the fold-C selection chose, used for the headline checks; every candidate's numbers are in `comparisons`, and `per_candidate_survival` says which candidates would have passed

R1b_residual_d.rule: in EVERY fold the residualised effect size is positive with a permutation z of at least +3.0

R2_mouth_specific.rule: the mouth's conditional AUC exceeds the cheek's by >= 0.02 with a paired permutation z of at least +2.0

R3_beats_head_motion.rule: macro_frame_recall margin >= 0.05 AND at least 2 of 3 folds where the mouth's session accuracy is >= the head's

R5_honesty_gate.why: the audio and the video of A/B/C are independent takes: no lag in +/-20 s and no video time base in 10-60 Hz aligns them (docs/research/NV12-STRIDE.md §6, docs/research/MOUTH-APERTURE-ALIGNMENT.md §4.3). Every evaluation here is therefore a SESSION-LEVEL statement, and the labels are session-level.

session_level_metric_is_degenerate.note: a predictor that identifies the SESSION rather than the speaking state can score 1.000 on this metric, so a leave-one-session-out accuracy is not on its own evidence of a mouth detector

reasons: R1 passes but R2 FAILS: the mouth feature's conditional AUC 0.7086 does not exceed the cheek control's 0.7443 by the required 0.02 (difference -0.0356, paired permutation z -1.70).

R4 also FAILS: the mouth feature's macro frame recall 0.6655 does not clear every null (margins {'permuted_labels': -0.0005592841163311046, 'blank': -0.001119508205966957, 'session_fingerprint': 0.33221382512736636}).
verdict.rule: The verdict is the FIRST of these that applies, and it is computed mechanically from the recorded control numbers: 1. if NOT (R1a AND R1b) -> 'mouth_signal_does_not_survive_head_motion'; 2. elif NOT R2 -> 'mouth_signal_survives_but_is_not_mouth_specific'; 3. elif NOT R3 -> 'mouth_detector_does_not_beat_head_motion'; 4. elif NOT R4 -> 'mouth_detector_beats_nothing'; 5. else -> 'mouth_detector_survives_head_motion'. If the data are insufficient to evaluate any check, the verdict is 'UNDETERMINED' and is never printed from a partial run.
verdict.scope: SESSION-LEVEL only. No frame-level speaking claim is made or supported by this lane.

supersedes.why: This lane re-tests, under a head-motion control, the mouth effect published in docs/research/NV12-STRIDE.md §5 and the falsification in docs/research/MOUTH-APERTURE-ALIGNMENT.md §4.2. Nothing is overwritten: the earlier numbers are reproduced here and their status is stated.

claims_under_test.claim: the mouth box moves more than the cheek when the wearer speaks: +0.733 sd at the mouth against +0.477 sd at the cheek, a 1.54x ratio, permutation z +10.9
claims_under_test.status: CONFIRMED, not withdrawn. Re-measured here with the same statistic: mouth A-C +0.7944 (+0.8279 sd) against cheek +0.3281 (+0.5398 sd), a ratio of 1.5337x on the 30 fps grid as recorded (published 1.54x) and 1.7881x on the distinct frames. The empty room carries 0.0093% of the mouth region's motion (published 0.015%). It is also STRENGTHENED by this lane's duplicate-frame correction and it SURVIVES the head-motion control (conditional AUC 0.7086, permutation z +9.60), which the earlier document did not test.

claims_under_test.claim: the mouth aperture's correlation with the speech envelope is about head motion, not the mouth: mouth width +0.3038 and head height +0.3316 beat the aperture's +0.2052
claims_under_test.status: NOT CONTRADICTED, because the statistic is different: that lane correlates the mouth's geometry with the AUDIO envelope frame by frame (which cannot be aligned here), while this lane asks whether the mouth region separates the two TAKES at matched head motion. On this lane's question the raw-luma mouth signal SURVIVES the head-motion control, and it does NOT beat its spatial control (R2 false) nor a constant predictor (R4 false).

not_superseded: the frame-level limit: the audio and the video of A/B/C are independent takes, so no frame-level audio<->video label is recoverable. This lane does not revisit it and does not contradict it.
